title: YouTube Shorts Hook Ideas: 50 Openers Built for Loops, Vertical Frames, and the Swipe
markdown:
# YouTube Shorts Hook Ideas: 50 Openers Built for Loops, Vertical Frames, and the Swipe

If you searched for "youtube shorts hook ideas," you are probably staring at a Shorts analytics screen where too many people swiped away before your video got going. This page gives you 50 hook ideas written for how Shorts actually plays: vertical, full-screen, one swipe from the next video, and looping when it ends.

Each hook has three parts:

- **Spoken:** what you say in the first three seconds, about 12 words or fewer.
- **On-screen:** the text overlay inside the frame. This is not your Shorts title, which sits below the frame.
- **Type:** one of five hook types, so you can test them against each other instead of guessing.

The five types:

- **Curiosity:** opens a question the viewer wants closed ("The one cable I'll never travel without").
- **Contrarian:** pushes against common advice ("Stop charging your phone overnight to 100%").
- **Stakes:** names a cost of ignoring the video ("This setting is quietly draining your battery").
- **Result:** leads with an outcome you actually got, using your real number.
- **Callout:** names the viewer directly ("Teachers with 30 kids, try this").

Where a hook needs a figure, it shows `[ADD: your number]`. Use only a number you can verify. If you don't have one, pick a different type.

**A note on loops:** a Short replays automatically. Write the last line so it flows back into the first. Several hooks below are marked as loop-friendly for that reason.

---

   **Type:** Callout

   **Type:** Result

## How to Choose and Test Your Shorts Hooks

**Choose**
- **Put the hook in the first frame, not after an intro.** On Shorts the video starts playing as soon as it appears. A logo, a "hey everyone," or a slow pan spends seconds you don't have.
- **Frame for vertical.** Keep your face, hands, or the key object in the middle of the 9:16 frame. Text placed too low can sit behind the title and channel name; text placed too far right can sit behind the like and comment buttons.
- **Split the job between title and overlay.** The Shorts title is what shows in search and under the player. Make it clear and searchable ("Peel garlic in 10 seconds"). Let the on-screen text carry the tension ("No knife needed").
- **Write for the loop.** If your last line hands off naturally to your first, a replay feels intentional instead of repetitive.
- **Use real numbers only.** A result hook built on a made-up number damages trust fast.

**Test**
1. Pick one video idea and write three hooks of different types.
2. Film the body once. Re-record only the opening for each version.
3. Publish the versions on different days at a similar time so the hook is the main variable.
4. In YouTube Studio, open each Short's analytics and compare the share of viewers who **viewed versus swiped away**, plus average view duration. Record the numbers: `[ADD: your result]`.
5. After several rounds, note which hook type wins most often for your channel and use it more, while still testing one new type regularly.

## FAQ

**What makes a good YouTube Shorts hook?**
A clear promise in the first second or two, shown on screen and said out loud, that the rest of the Short actually delivers. Specific objects and actions ("peel a whole bulb of garlic") tend to read faster than abstract claims ("cooking tips").

**Is the Shorts title the same as the hook?**
No. The title sits under the video and in search results, so write it to be clear and searchable. The hook is the first spoken line and the on-screen text inside the frame. They should support each other without repeating word for word.

**What does "viewed vs swiped away" mean in Shorts analytics?**
It's the split YouTube Studio shows between people who stayed to watch your Short and people who swiped to the next video when it appeared in their feed. It's the most direct readout of how your opening performed, so compare it across hook versions.

**Can I reuse TikTok or Reels hooks on Shorts?**
Yes, the first-seconds principle is the same. Check that overlay text clears Shorts' title, channel name, and side buttons, and adjust the title for search, since Shorts titles are visible in YouTube search results.
